_charter.job: For each surviving candidate (post audience_modeler kill-recommendations), specify the exact predict, kill_condition, and apoha. Compute sha256_pre_verdict over the triple. The seam-1 SEAL fires here — frozen-at-emission.
_charter.refuses: vague predicts. A predict like 'this will be useful' is REJECTED — must be a specific observable outcome with a checkable threshold. A kill_condition like 'people don't like it' is REJECTED — must be concrete + measurable. An empty apoha is REJECTED — minimum 1 inverted-kill required.
apoha: NOT optimistic-flag-on-acceptance ('if at least one person likes it')
NOT shipping a seal without a sha256 over the sealed triple
NOT softening apoha into the positive-frame ('it WILL be X') — the inverted-kill must REMAIN inverted
_charter.method: For surviving candidate c: predict = 'WITHIN <window>, OBSERVABLE <signal> MEETS <threshold>'; kill_condition = 'IF <observable> < <threshold> BY <date>, this idea is FALSIFIED'; apoha = [array of >=1 'NOT X' statements]. sha256_pre_verdict = sha256(canonical_json({candidate_id, predict, kill_condition, apoha})). Seal fires at emission; sha is immutable thereafter.

_note: Maps to miles's universal `problem-definer` phase-agent. The seal mechanism is structurally identical to the bootstrap standard's seam-1 (charter seal). When miles ships, this agent's seal-discipline pattern can collapse into the universal phase-agent's seal hook.
